exposure: socioeconomic characteristics (ethnic minorities, rural residences, low education)
outcome: indications for cesarean delivery (nonreassuring fetal status, labor arrest, fetal malpresentation, cephalopelvic disproportion)
cohort: The study included 432 adolescent pregnant women (10-19 years) and 432 adult pregnant women (20-34 years) hospitalized for delivery at Can Tho Gynecology Obstetrics Hospital.
finding: Adolescent pregnancies were associated with more adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes compared to adult pregnancies.
mod_finding: Adolescents had a higher proportion of cesarean deliveries due to nonreassuring fetal status and labor arrest, but lower proportions due to fetal malpresentation and cephalopelvic disproportion, compared to adults.
